extractions.quote: This patient had classic findings of stiff-man syndrome. EMG studies were normal except for continuous motor unit activity, mainly in the paraspinous muscles. Exaggerated exteroceptive reflex responses were elicited. Both exteroceptive reflexes and continuous motor unit activity were abolished or markedly reduced following intravenous infusion of 10 mg diazepam. Indirect immunofluorescent screening of serum revealed autoantibody reactive with normal human cerebellum in a pattern consistent with GABAergic terminals.

extractions.value: Exteroceptive reflexes were recorded using a modification of the technique described by Meinck et al. Surface recordings were made simultaneously from five muscle groups (abductor pollicis brevis, biceps brachii, lumbar paraspinal, biceps femoris, and tibialis anterior) using a TECA Mystro EMG. The recording gain was adjusted to obtain a well-defined signal from each channel. A frequency window of 20 Hz to 2,000 Hz was used in all recordings. The responses were full-wave-rectified and four responses were signal-averaged. Each response was obtained by delivering a train of five stimuli to the median nerve at the wrist at a rate of 200 Hz. The stimulus was delivered at the threshold for motor activation of the thenar muscles.
